Deaf man with a speech impediment
Boy possessed by an unclean spirit
entries.editorialNote: Mark 9:29 starts the onward journey through Galilee in all three pinned witnesses; the healing and explanation end at verse 28.

entries.readerTitle: Healing of the blind man near Jericho

entries.editorialNote: Matthew 13:36–43 contains Christ's explanation of the wheat and tares; Matthew 13:31–35 is different intervening teaching.
Read the rich man and Lazarus only in Luke's terms: no confident inference about the historical identity of the characters.

entries.readerTitle: The last judgment: sheep and goats
entries.editorialNote: The Last Judgment is presented as future; do not date it as a narrated past earthly event.
The cleansing of the Temple (Mark 11:15–19) intervenes between the fig-tree action and recognition of its withering.

entries.readerTitle: Debates and denunciations involving the authorities
entries.editorialNote: Matthew 21:1–22 includes the Jerusalem entry and Temple actions; Matthew 22:1–14 is a separate indexed wedding parable. Matthew 23 is a public denunciation, not another question-and-answer debate.
John 15 also includes the hatred of the world and the testimony of the Spirit, not only the vine image.
